subject: Fincobank - audit logs & data access follow-up
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.m@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@fincobank.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@fincobank.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Fincobank - audit logs & data access follow-up

Hi Tom / Aisha -

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the action items we discussed related to audit logging and data access:

- Primary asks from your security/compliance team: extractable audit logs showing "who accessed what/when" for customer data, exportable in a standard format for internal retention and audits.
- Key fields you mentioned: user identifier, action, resource, timestamp, IP/source, session id, and any query parameters.
- Requirements to confirm: retention window (you mentioned 7 years as a possibility), export formats (CSV/JSON/Parquet), and whether logs must be redacted/hashed for PII before export.
- Residency: confirm whether all exported evidence must remain in us-east-1 (you mentioned possible EU residency for some customers).

Next steps I promised: provide a short evidence pack (schema + sample export), confirm export APIs and bulk export cadence, and schedule a technical follow-up with our security/ops lead. I'll also include notes on RBAC, key management, and how we record operator access to the export process.

I'm attaching a sample schema (audit_log_schema.csv) and a redacted sample access report (access_report_2026-08-10.json) for reference - these are representative exports from a recent audit so you can confirm fields.

If anything I captured above is incorrect, flag it and I'll adjust. Otherwise, could you confirm the retention window you need and whether the team prefers CSV vs JSON/Parquet for ingestion into your internal systems?

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.m@redwood.com

---
Attachments: audit_log_schema.csv (CSV), access_report_2026-08-10.json (JSON, redacted sample)

From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@fincobank.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.m@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@fincobank.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Fincobank - audit logs & data access follow-up

Alex -

Thanks for the summary and the samples - very helpful. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Required fields: we need at minimum: user_id (email or internal id), action (read/write/export/delete), resource (document/model/request id), timestamp (ISO8601), source_ip, session_id, request_payload_hash (if possible), and response_status.
2) Retention: regulatory wants us to keep audit logs for 7 years for certain transaction types - we may flag a subset that requires longer retention. Can Redwood support configurable retention per-account or per-log-type?
3) Export formats: CSV would be easiest for our legacy tooling, but we'd prefer JSON or Parquet for big-batch ingestion. Ideally support all three (CSV/JSON/Parquet).
4) Access patterns: we'd like both ad hoc query/API access for investigations and periodic bulk exports (daily/weekly/monthly).
5) PII: for exports we need options - full anonymization/hashing for certain fields, and a redacted export mode that removes user-identifiable fields.
6) Evidence chain: for audits we need a tamper-evident export (signed export or hash) and an operator access log that shows which Redwood personnel accessed the export and when.

Also, can you send your standard DPA and SOC2 report (or SOC2 audit letter) for procurement? Our procurement contact will want to see those attachments.

Available for a technical follow-up tomorrow between 10–12 PT if that works for your security ops folks.

Thanks,
Tom
Senior InfoSec Manager, FinCoBank

From: Alex Martinez <alex.m@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@fincobank.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@fincobank.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Fincobank - audit logs & data access follow-up

Tom -

Appreciate the clear list. Quick responses inline and attached files:

- Fields: yes - we can produce the fields you listed. The attached audit_log_schema.csv maps each field to column names and notes whether a field is optional or always present.
- Retention: Redwood supports configurable retention policies at the account and log-type level; we can set minimum retention to 7 years for the flagged transaction types and shorter for debug-level logs. We'll include guidance on export sizes and storage cost impacts.
- Export formats: we support CSV, newline-delimited JSON, and Parquet for bulk exports. API queries return JSON; bulk exports can be pushed to an S3 bucket you control or pulled via a signed URL.
- Access patterns: we have a Query API for ad hoc investigation (RBAC enforced), and a Bulk Export API with signed manifests. Bulk exports are time-window based and can be generated on demand or scheduled.
- PII/redaction: we support field-level redaction (hashing/pseudonymization), a redacted export mode, and a policy-based redaction pipeline. We will document which fields are non-reversibly hashed vs tokenized.
- Evidence chain: exports include a manifest file with SHA256 checksums and an audit of who initiated the export; operator access to the export system is logged and included in the evidence pack.

Attached:
- audit_log_schema.csv - column definitions and examples
- access_report_2026-08-10.json - a redacted sample export (matches schema)

Next steps (proposed):
1) Confirm retention windows per log-type and whether S3 export must stay in us-east-1 only or we should support eu-west-1 for EU-resident data.
2) Technical follow-up with our security/ops: Jordan (security) and Marissa (customer success/ops) - proposed window tomorrow 10-11 PT.
3) I will also drop our DPA/SOC2 summary link in this thread for procurement.

Can you confirm the retention windows and preferred export format? Once you confirm, Marissa will prepare the formal evidence pack and Jordan will provide the SOC2/DPA references.

Best,
Alex

---
Attachments: audit_log_schema.csv, access_report_2026-08-10.json
Related: https://docs.redwood.com/security/audit-logs#evidence-pack

From: Alex Martinez <alex.m@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-16T08:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Fincobank - audit logs & data access follow-up

Marissa / Jordan -

Forwarding FinCo's reply and the sample artifacts. Action items to prepare the evidence pack:

- Marissa: please prepare a redwood export sample that includes the full manifest (SHA256), the operator-access log (who generated the export & timestamp), and a scheduled bulk export job (daily) demo. Target delivery: 2026-08-18 EOD. Attach the actual sample files to the Drive folder linked below.

- Jordan: can you pull the SOC2 summary + DPA link and a short note on our tamper-evidence approach (signed manifests, checksums, and access audit)? We should include exact RBAC roles that can initiate exports and how to map them to FinCo roles.

- Alex: I'll schedule the technical call for tomorrow 10-11 PT; invite includes Tom and Aisha.

Let me know if the delivery dates are tight. I'll also confirm whether FinCo requires all exports to remain in us-east-1 or if they need EU residency for some accounts.

Thanks,
Alex
